factor_diagnostics.value_notes: A juvenile red snapper habitat-suitability study in the northwestern Gulf found high-value habitat at bottom temperatures of 24–26 °C. NOAA acoustic telemetry off North Carolina found red snapper movement related to bottom-water temperature and vertical thermotaxis. These are juvenile or regional bottom-water relationships, not a universal surface-temperature preference curve; they do not directly validate the configured 16–26 °C range or 19–23 °C ideal.
